title: Polycrisis Resilience: Origin, Definition and Formal Framework
subtitle: The Foundational Statement of a Framework for Reducing Human and Systemic Vulnerability to Interacting Crises, With Its Definition, Architecture, Tools and Documented Origin
description: Polycrisis Resilience is the capacity of individuals, communities, institutions, economies, societies and interconnected systems to anticipate, withstand…
contribution: The foundational statement of Polycrisis Resilience: canonical clause-by-clause definition, six-capacity architecture, Preventive Development mechanism, four operational tools, eight testable propositions, and graded two-layer documentary origin and attribution record.
abstract: Foundational hybrid academic paper and attribution record for Polycrisis Resilience (HH-2026-93, 38 pages), authored by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (ORCID 0009-0002-6161-9387).

keyFindings.title: Definition: Resilience as a capacity with five verbs, the fifth being reduce vulnerability; interacting crises as the unit of analysis.
Framework: Six properties, six capacities (risk reduction, preventive, absorptive, recovery, adaptive, transformative), four drivers, five systems, five-stage cycle.
Mechanism: Preventive Development—everyday investments in energy, water, health and connectivity lower exposure and fragility in advance, for all hazards at once.
Tools: 5×5×5 matrix, six-question Test (with proposed scoring), weakest-link indicators, Polycrisis Risk Reduction Index.
Origin: First dated public formalization March 2025 (Hughes); fixed DOI-registered record October–November 2026.
Boundary: A proposed framework open to testing.
keyFindings.text: The report claims origination of the framework, not invention of the word polycrisis and not empirical proof.
